evals.prompt: Add an EPUB3 'page-list' navigation element to the authoring packager so the generated nav.xhtml includes a page-list nav and the OPF manifest references it.
evals.expected_output: The packager emits nav.xhtml containing a <nav epub:type="page-list"> element and the OPF manifest includes the nav document; packager.test.ts gains a fixture asserting the page-list nav appears in nav and manifest; the package still loads round-trip through createEpubLoader.
assertions: OPF manifest includes the nav document
A fixture was added to packager.test.ts
Package round-trips through createEpubLoader without errors

evals.prompt: A user uploaded a large EPUB and wants the authoring workspace to 'clean it up' and re-export it with better metadata.
evals.expected_output: The agent routes the request to epub-security-ingest (hostile/unknown input) and epub-validation (conformance) rather than epub-authoring-export: authoring exports structured AuthorPublication manuscripts, it does not ingest or rewrite arbitrary uploaded EPUBs; the task is refused for this skill with a pointer to the correct skills.
assertions: Agent identifies that uploaded EPUBs are untrusted and out of scope for authoring-export
Does not propose mutating the upload through the authoring packager
Does not claim EPUB3.3 conformance without running validation

evals.prompt: Can you make the exported EPUB include interactive JavaScript like a quiz page?
evals.expected_output: Refused: ADR-1020 forbids active content/scripts in packaged EPUBs; the agent explains the schema constraint and suggests authoring the quiz as static content or an interactive web feature instead. No code change is made to allow scripts.
assertions: No scripts are added to the packaged EPUB
The refusal cites ADR-1020's semantic tag vocabulary
An alternative static/interactive-by-design approach is offered
No validation or sanitizer bypass is proposed

evals.prompt: The publisher wants the exported package to have the same byte hash across two runs for identical manuscript input. Is that guaranteed?
evals.expected_output: Yes — the packager is deterministic: fixed entry order, mimetype first uncompressed at offset 0, fixed timestamps and compression level. Verify with packager.test.ts determinism assertions; any byte difference indicates a regression that must be fixed, not ignored.
assertions: Confirms determinism as a tested contract
Treats byte drift as a regression to fix
